## Scope Assessment

When the user requests a **TASK**, evaluate whether it is actually EPIC-sized before creating it. Look for these signals:

- Multiple distinct steps or deliverables in the description
- Multiple action verbs joined by "and" (e.g., "add auth and set up roles and integrate SSO")
- Work that spans different code areas or concerns
- Sub-steps that could be completed and shipped independently

**Quick test:** "Could someone meaningfully complete and ship part of this while the rest remains undone?" If yes → likely an EPIC.

If EPIC signals are present, suggest an EPIC + sub-TASKs with a concrete breakdown. For example:

> "This looks like it has multiple independent deliverables. Want me to create an EPIC with separate TASKs for each piece instead?"

**This is a soft suggestion only.** If the user says "just make it a task," comply without pushback.

This assessment only applies to TASK creation — do not second-guess EPICs, NOTEs, or other types.

## Arguments

The user provides the type and title: `/board:board-add task <title>`, `/board:board-add epic <title>`, etc.

If no type is given, ask the user what type of item to create.

## Determine Next ID

Run the ID assignment script:

```bash
bash "/Users/grant/.claude/plugins/cache/gdkeller/board/0.1.0/scripts/next-id.sh" <TYPE> ./board
```

## Create the File

Use the correct directory, frontmatter, and naming convention:

| Type | Directory | Filename Example |
|------|-----------|-----------------|
| task | `board/tasks/` | `TASK-0014_add-batch-processing.md` |
| epic | `board/planning/` | `EPIC-0009_batch-mode.md` |
| adr | `board/planning/` | `ADR-0002_chose-webgpu-over-wasm.md` |
| note | `board/planning/` | `NOTE-0001_explore-wasm-option.md` |
| reference | `board/reference/` | `REFE-0007_webgpu-overview.md` |
| resource | `board/resources/` | `RESO-0001_webgpu-article.md` |

## Frontmatter Templates

Task:
```yaml
---
type: task
status: backlog
priority: 2
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

Epic:
```yaml
---
type: epic
status: planning
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

ADR:
```yaml
---
type: adr
status: active
context_date: YYYY-MM-DD
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

Note:
```yaml
---
type: note
status: inbox
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

Reference:
```yaml
---
type: reference
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

Resource (ask user for URL):
```yaml
---
type: resource
status: inbox
url: <url>
created: YYYY-MM-DD
---
```

## Naming Rules

- Convert title to kebab-case for filename
- Task titles MUST be imperative mood (start with a verb). If the user gives a noun phrase, rewrite it (e.g., "batch processing" -> "Add batch processing support")
- Use today's date for `created`

## After Creation

Show the file path and ask if the user wants to add more detail to the body.

```text
# EPIC-0020: Layout & visual polish

A backlog of small visual and layout refinements from internal review and external critique. Two reviewers independently flagged the same five issues — orphaned palette strip, dead space under the grid, blended Export button, invisible Compare disclosure, missing favicon — plus a handful of smaller affordance polish items. Each is small in isolation; bundling lets the work happen as a coherent polish pass.

## Goals

- Resolve the high-overlap issues from NOTE-0010 / NOTE-0011.
- Tighten small interaction affordances (swatch hover, copy feedback, hue-dot connection, toggle states).
- Lock down typography and radius decisions deferred since launch.

## Tasks

- TASK-0095 — Add context label to PaletteStrip full-scale gradient
- TASK-0096 — Resolve vertical dead space below palette grid in row layout
- TASK-0097 — Bump Export button visual weight
- TASK-0098 — Add static favicon assets *(archived 2026-05-07 as done; NOTE-0010 #5 was stale, work already shipped)*
- TASK-0099 — Make Compare disclosure visible
- TASK-0100 — Improve swatch-label legibility on mid-tone backgrounds
- TASK-0101 — Polish small interaction affordances (hue dot, toggle, swatch hover)
- TASK-0102 — Redesign swatch copy-feedback overlay
- TASK-0103 — Evaluate refined typography and tighten border radii
- TASK-0121 — Adopt a mono typeface for color values and code

- NOTE-0012 — UX & interaction ideas (font / radius items)
- NOTE-0018 — Improve swatch copy feedback
- NOTE-0027 — Rethink swatch hover state
```

```text
export function ChartTabs({ entries }: ChartTabsProps) {
  const [showDots, setShowDots] = useState(true);
  const [showCompare, setShowCompare] = useState(false);
  const hue = usePaletteStore((s) => s.hue);
  const saturation = usePaletteStore((s) => s.saturation);

  const { unadjustedColors, adjustedColors } = useMemo(
    () => ({
      unadjustedColors: entries.map((e) =>
        chroma.hsl(hue, saturation, e.lightness / 100).hex(),
      ),
      adjustedColors: entries.map((e) => e.hex),
    }),
    [entries, hue, saturation],
  );

  return (
    <div className="border-border-default bg-surface-raised mx-4 overflow-hidden rounded-none border md:mx-0 lg:mr-4">
      <div className="flex items-center justify-between px-4 py-2 md:hidden lg:flex">

          Saturation Curve
        </h2>

          <Tabs.Trigger
          Compare
        </button>
        <ToggleSwitch label="steps" checked={showDots} onChange={setShowDots} />
      </div>
      {showCompare && (
        <div className="space-y-2 px-4 pb-3 md:hidden lg:block">

            <span className="text-text-faint mb-1 block text-xs">
              Unadjusted

              ))}

          <div>
            <span className="text-text-faint mb-1 block text-xs">Adjusted</span>
            <div className="grid h-6 auto-cols-fr grid-flow-col overflow-hidden rounded-none">
              {adjustedColors.map((c, i) => (
                <div key={i} style={{ backgroundColor: c }} />
              ))}
            </div>
          </div>
        </div>
      )}
    </div>
  );
}

# TASK-0099: Make Compare disclosure visible

The "Compare" disclosure currently uses `text-text-faint` with no caret or hover state, so it reads as ambient text rather than an interactive affordance. Users miss it entirely.

## Acceptance

- Compare disclosure uses a stronger text token (`text-text-muted` or `text-text-secondary`).
- Hover/focus state visibly distinguishes it from static text.
- Caret or chevron icon clarifies expandable behavior.
- Optionally: default to expanded so the comparison is always visible (decide during implementation).

## Source

- NOTE-0010 (#3), NOTE-0011

## Related

- TASK-0083 — unadjusted reference strip; pairs with this disclosure's contents.
```

```text
export function generateNeutrals(params: PaletteParams): ColorEntry[] {
  const { hue, saturation, sMod, satMode, lMin, lMax } = params;

  const entries: ColorEntry[] = [];

  for (let i = lMin; i <= lMax; i++) {
    const l = i / 100;
    const sK = getSaturation(i, sMod, satMode);
    const color = chroma.hsl(hue, saturation * sK, l);

    const [h, s, lVal] = color.hsl();
    const hRound = Math.round(h) || 0;
    const sRound = Math.round(s * 10000) / 100;
    const lRound = Math.round(lVal * 10000) / 100;

    entries.push({
      label: `grey-${i}`,
      lightness: i,
      hsl: [h, s, lVal],
      hslString: `${hRound} ${sRound}% ${lRound}%`,
      hex: color.hex(),
    });
  }

  return entries.reverse();
}
```

```markdown
# TASK-0130: Align Compare strips with the chart's lightness axis

The Saturation Curve chart plots lightness 0 → 100 left to right, but the Unadjusted and Adjusted strips in the Compare disclosure directly below it run white → black (100 → 0). Reading the strip against the curve above it requires mentally flipping one of them, which breaks the "show the math" link between the two.

## Cause

`generateNeutrals()` (`app/src/lib/palette.ts`) returns entries light → dark (`entries.reverse()`). `ChartTabs` (`app/src/components/ChartTabs/ChartTabs.tsx`) maps `entries` straight into both strips, so they inherit that order. `PaletteStrip` already reverses the entries locally for its own dark → light display.

## Acceptance

- Both Compare strips run dark → light (L0 on the left), matching the chart's x-axis.
- Fix lives in `ChartTabs` (reverse locally, as `PaletteStrip` does); `generateNeutrals()` output order is unchanged, since `PaletteGrid`, export, and others depend on it.
- Decide whether the strips should also span the chart's full 0–100 axis when `lMin`/`lMax` narrow the range (currently they cover only `lMin..lMax`, so they no longer line up with the axis ticks). Options: pad/offset the strip to the plotted range, or leave as-is and accept a stretched strip.

## Related

- TASK-0099 — Make Compare disclosure visible (same component, natural to pair)
- TASK-0083 — unadjusted reference strip
```
